name: Mickel Therapy
founders: David Mickel, MD (medical doctor per own site; 'former Scottish GP' per secondary accounts, unverified)
founded_year_range: 1999-2001 (estimate: site claims 'over 25 years' of work as of 2026; no founding year stated; early-2000s UK presence and c.2002 Reverse Therapy spin-off are unverified background)
category: limbic/brain retraining course (practitioner coaching; historical precursor)
cost_summary: Verified Oct 2026: Self-Directed Core Course GBP 295; Guided Core Course GBP 595 (or 3 x GBP 205), which includes 3 team-coach sessions within 9 months; Personal Guidance with Dr Mickel GBP 2,195 (core course, 3 private sessions within 6 months, 6 months of messaging); individual consultations with Mickel are unpriced; workshop membership GBP 20; coach certification GBP 1,495 (two training weekends; core course is a separate prerequisite). Donation-funded bursaries are available through the Vitality Foundation.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
emotional awareness / unexpressed present-day feelings (symptoms as signals)
mechanism_summary: The original model was 'hypothalamitis', and the program now calls it the 'Prolonged Activation State' (PAS). In this model, feelings that arise from present-day interactions are repeatedly overridden or left unanswered, and each new situation adds fresh activation. The hypothalamus, described on the site as the coordinating centre for the nervous, endocrine and immune systems, is said to stay 'on' as a result, producing fatigue, pain, brain fog, sensitivities and immune or allergy-type ('MCAS-type') symptoms. An infection can start the process, but PAS is explicitly 'not the residue of that event' and is not framed as past trauma or repressed emotion. Symptoms are treated as messages that call for a response. One model covers all of the conditions the program claims to treat.
techniques: notice feelings and symptoms as signals/messages
link the feeling to a current situation or relationship
take concrete responsive action (assertion, boundaries, expressing needs) instead of overriding
'Feeling vs Story': separating the felt signal from the mental narrative
5-module, 17-lesson self-paced online core course with worksheets
1:1 coach sessions (3 in the guided track)
historically: a short series of practitioner sessions with symptom/feeling diary homework (unverified)
mainstream_notes: There is no NHS commissioning, guideline endorsement or academic program. NICE CG53 (2007) and NG206 (2021) do not recommend it. NG206 warns against the Lightning Process and therapies based on it but does not name Mickel Therapy. Coaches are certified only by the company, through two training weekends plus a one-month check-in.
insurance_notes: Self-pay only. No insurer coverage or billing codes were found, and coaches are not a regulated profession.
controversy: 'Hypothalamitis' is a real but rare diagnosis of autoimmune or inflammatory hypothalamic lesions, and the PubMed literature on it consists of case reports such as anti-Ma hypothalamitis. Applying the term to ME/CFS has no evidential basis, and the program has since replaced it with PAS. ME/CFS patient advocates group Mickel Therapy with the Lightning Process and Reverse Therapy as unproven commercial coaching that implies patients sustain their illness through emotional habits; a critical 2011 reader comment on the ME Association site is one example. The site cites no studies, and testimonials stand in for outcome data, despite marketing to people with post-viral illness, including long COVID.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 5,000-20,000 people over 25 years. Basis: the site's 'thousands' claim, a niche UK/Commonwealth practitioner network, and a small online-course business. Low confidence.
popularity.method_notes: The web-search budget ran out in both the research pass and the fact-check pass, so news archives, Reddit, Wayback, Google Trends and YouTube metrics could not be retrieved. The trajectory is a qualitative reconstruction: development c.1999-2001; a 2000s UK peak alongside the Lightning Process and Reverse Therapy (unverified background); decline in the 2010s; a modest long-COVID-driven online relaunch from 2020. All values have low confidence.
